policy.why: Uniform for comparisons: each provider answers with the model it was asked for. Only Anthropic offers a server-side model fallback, so enabling it would credit Claude with other models' output.

cli.why: Subscription baseline without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: Claude Code headless (-p), same prompt, schema and model.

claude.source: claude-api skill model table (cached 2026-10-06); no vendor page fetched

cli.why: Subscription baseline without OPENAI_API_KEY: Codex exec on the ChatGPT login, same models (gpt-6.1-terra and gpt-6-luna verified there 2026-11-04).

chatgpt.source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna; gpt-6.1-terra verified only via Codex on the ChatGPT login

cli.why: Subscription baseline without a Gemini key: agy print mode, Flash 3.8 at low effort for both profiles. With thinking on, agy returns an empty response (verified 2026-11-04).
Subscription baseline without XAI_API_KEY: grok -p on the xAI session. The session offers grok-4.7 but not the API realtime model, so realtime uses its fast model (verified 2026-11-04).

grok.source: https://docs.x.ai/developers/models (lists both ids; states no latency, so the non-reasoning model is a latency choice, not a documented tier)

muse.source: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models (muse-spark-1.3 recommended for new work; 1.1 still listed)
muse.note: Meta lists no faster Spark tier, so both profiles use muse-spark-1.3 and differ only by reasoning_effort. Realtime is minimal, the lowest effort Spark accepts (none is a 400): 9.5, 7.2 and 6.2 s on three corpus prompts, all valid, against a ~15 s median at low (measured 2026-11-04).
